records.name: First Friend
records.flavor: You saw it through — gathered, built, shaped the land, and welcomed your first neighbor. A single hop in the grass, and you already know how to bring back a whole meadow.
records.hint: Every caretaker's journey begins with one small arrival.

records.name: Forager
records.flavor: A hundred fallen things picked up and put to use. You've stopped scrounging and started stockpiling.
records.hint: Gather, and keep gathering — build a real stockpile.

records.name: Maker's Hands
records.flavor: Ten things built by hand. Habitat isn't found — it's made, one piece at a time.
records.hint: Keep crafting; one item won't restore a meadow.

records.name: Green Thumb
records.flavor: Ten living things in soil you readied yourself. Half of restoration is just patience with a watering can.
records.hint: Put down roots — plant, and plant again.

records.name: Waterworks
records.flavor: Beds dug, ground watered, the first pools shaped. Wet ground is the difference between bare dirt and a place that holds life.
records.hint: Work the soil and bring it water, again and again.

records.name: First Bloom
records.flavor: Grasshopper, then a bee, then a sparrow that eats both, then a fox that eats the sparrow. A food web is just neighbors who need each other.
records.hint: Coax the meadow well past its first lonely visitor.

records.name: Pollinator Highway
records.flavor: Monarch, bumblebee, leafcutter, lady beetle, painted lady — the unpaid workforce that turns flowers into seeds and seeds into more meadow.
records.hint: Bring back the meadow's little winged workforce.

records.name: Apex of the Grass
records.flavor: A fox only settles where there are voles and rabbits to hunt — so its arrival means the whole chain beneath it is finally fed.
records.hint: A meadow is whole when its top hunter trusts it.

records.name: Meadow Mender
records.flavor: The dust is gone. Where you started there was bare ground; now there's a meadow that hums.
records.hint: Heal Willow Meadow most of the way back.

records.name: Willow Meadow Reborn
records.flavor: Every animal that belongs here is home. The meadow doesn't need you to hum anymore — but it remembers who started it.
records.hint: Leave no meadow animal behind.

records.name: Understory Returns
records.flavor: Ferns, shrubs, a squirrel arguing with a woodpecker, newts under the deadwood. A forest is built from the ground up, not the canopy down.
records.hint: Rebuild the forest floor, layer by layer.

records.name: Hollow Dwellers
records.flavor: The big woodpecker carves a hole, uses it once, and leaves it for everyone else. One bird's old home is another's new one.
records.hint: Some birds carve homes that others move into — gather that crowd.

records.name: Night Shift
records.flavor: After dark a second forest wakes up. The owl hunts what the day birds never see, and the skunk turns over the leaf litter for grubs.
records.hint: Wake the forest that only stirs after dark.

records.name: Canopy Restored
records.flavor: Shade on the forest floor again. The big trees you raised will outlive everyone reading their rings.
records.hint: Raise Old Hollow Forest most of the way back.

records.name: Old Hollow Forest Reborn
records.flavor: From a logged-over silence to a full, layered wood — floor, understory, canopy, and every wing in between.
records.hint: Leave no forest animal behind.

records.name: Water Returns
records.flavor: Shape the water and the water brings its own crowd — frogs, striders, dragonflies skating the surface, a heron stalking the shallows.
records.hint: Shape water, and life will find it.

records.name: The Engineer
records.flavor: The beaver doesn't move into habitat — it builds it. One dam, and otters, herons, and frogs all get a home they couldn't have made themselves.
records.hint: Welcome the one who builds habitat for everyone else.

records.name: Lakemaker
records.flavor: Enough open water to hold a sky. Turtles bask, mergansers dive, and the whole marsh has a center again.
records.hint: Open enough connected water to hold a sky.

records.name: Marsh Restored
records.flavor: Reeds where there was cracked mud, channels that actually flow. A wetland filters everything downstream of it — quiet, unpaid work.
records.hint: Heal Rushwater Wetland most of the way back.

records.name: Rushwater Wetland Reborn
records.flavor: Crane to minnow, the whole drained marsh is wet and loud and alive.
records.hint: Leave no wetland animal behind.

records.name: Life in the Heat
records.flavor: Out here life hides from the sun, not in it. The brush and burrows you've built are the first shade anything's had in years.
records.hint: Give the heat something to hide in.

records.name: Burrow Network
records.flavor: In the desert, real estate is underground. A tortoise digs a burrow and an owl moves into the spare room — nobody wastes a hole here.
records.hint: In the desert, the right neighbors share their holes.

records.name: Dryland Hunter
records.flavor: A predator that can wait out the heat means there's finally enough prey to be patient for.
records.hint: A hunter that waits out the heat needs prey worth waiting for.

records.name: Scrubland Restored
records.flavor: Brush and cactus where there was overgrazed flat. You can't flood a desert back — you have to shade it back, and you did.
records.hint: Bring Redstone Scrubland most of the way back.

records.name: Redstone Scrubland Reborn
records.flavor: The hardest country in the preserve, fully alive — from the elf owl in the cactus to the tarantula under the stone.
records.hint: Leave no desert animal behind.

records.name: Above the Treeline
records.flavor: Nothing up here is here by accident. Every one of these has chosen the thin air on purpose.
records.hint: Coax the first hardy few above the trees.

records.name: The Haymaker
records.flavor: The pika spends all summer stacking little hay piles for a winter it refuses to sleep through. Tiny animal, enormous work ethic.
records.hint: Welcome the tireless little hay-stacker of the rocks.

records.name: Crown of the Range
records.flavor: When the eagle circles the ridge, the marmots whistle and the whole slope listens. The top of the food web has come home.
records.hint: Crown the range with its highest hunter.

records.name: Heights Restored
records.flavor: Wildflower turf knitted back over the talus. Up here things grow by the inch and recover by the decade — you sped it up.
records.hint: Bring Graywind Heights most of the way back.

records.name: Graywind Heights Reborn
records.flavor: Goat to ptarmigan to trout in the snowmelt — the whole high country, restored against the wind.
records.hint: Leave no alpine animal behind.

records.name: The Tide Returns
records.flavor: Crabs in the wrack line, anemones in the pools, gulls working the surf. The tide was always coming in — now there's a whole shore to meet it.
records.hint: Give the tide a shore worth returning to.

records.name: Keystone
records.flavor: The textbook keystone species: pull the sea star out and the mussels take everything. Put it back and the whole tidepool shares the rock again.
records.hint: Restore the one animal that holds the whole tidepool together.

records.name: Otter's Garden
records.flavor: Otters eat the urchins that eat the kelp — so an otter on the water means a forest under it. Few animals do more with a full belly.
records.hint: Welcome the swimmer that keeps the kelp standing.

records.name: Shore Restored
records.flavor: Anchored dunes, full tidepools, kelp in the wrack. The edge of the whole preserve, holding the line against the sea.
records.hint: Bring Pelican Shore most of the way back.

records.name: Pelican Shore Reborn
records.flavor: Whale-spout to clam-siphon. The last and wildest stretch of the preserve, complete.
records.hint: Leave no coastal animal behind.

records.name: Well Stocked
records.flavor: A thousand fallen things gathered. You stopped scrounging long ago — this is provisioning.
records.hint: Gather far past what any one project needs.

records.name: Master Builder
records.flavor: A hundred and fifty pieces of habitat, placed by hand. The whole preserve has your fingerprints on it.
records.hint: Place habitat until the whole preserve bears your hand.

records.name: Master Gardener
records.flavor: Seventy-five living things put in the ground, sprout by patient sprout. Restoration is mostly just showing up with a watering can.
records.hint: Plant on a scale that changes the land.

records.name: Landscaper
records.flavor: You don't find the right land — you shape it. Beds, banks, ponds, lakes, and rivers, all on purpose.
records.hint: Shape soil and water across the preserve, tirelessly.

records.name: Fully Equipped
records.flavor: Top-tier gear for top-tier work. There's nothing left in the preserve you can't carry, dig, or water.
records.hint: Carry your basket, shovel, and watering can to their peak.

records.name: Naturalist
records.flavor: Twelve books on the shelf — a guide to every area and the annotated edition beside it. You don't just host wildlife now, you understand it.
records.hint: Write up every area's field guide, and its expanded edition.

records.name: Recipe Collector
records.flavor: Seventy-five different things, each built at least once. You've used nearly every tool on the bench.
records.hint: Build a little of almost everything on the bench.

records.name: Open Road
records.flavor: The first trail gate swings open. One healed meadow, and the whole preserve starts to feel reachable.
records.hint: Heal one biome enough to open the next trail.

records.name: Welcoming Committee
records.flavor: Fifty species have decided this place is safe again. Word travels fast in the wild.
records.hint: Draw a real crowd back to the preserve.

records.name: Full House
records.flavor: A hundred kinds of neighbor. The preserve isn't recovering anymore — it's thriving.
records.hint: Fill the preserve with neighbors.

records.name: Field Notes
records.flavor: Page after page of observations. You don't just bring animals back — you sit with them long enough to learn who they are.
records.hint: Observe your wild neighbors, again and again, all over the preserve.

records.name: Steady Hand
records.flavor: No biome left to languish while you favored another. Every place you've opened is in good health at once.
records.hint: Keep every area you've opened in good health at the same time.

records.name: Halfway Wild
records.flavor: Three damaged places, brought most of the way home. The preserve is tipping from recovering to recovered.
records.hint: Bring several different biomes most of the way back.

records.name: Trailblazer
records.flavor: Every gate open, every trail walked. From your tent to the sea, it's all connected now.
records.hint: Open every trail in the preserve.

records.name: Caretaker of the Whole
records.flavor: Every animal in every biome, home. The damaged preserve you inherited is now, simply, wild. The rarest achievement there is.
records.hint: Welcome home every animal in every biome.
